about.title: Brentwood Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Brentwood's growth has brought heavier traffic to corridors like Balfour Road, Brentwood Boulevard, Sand Creek Road, and SR-4, and public collision counts show a steady number of injury crashes each year, with Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. seeing more reported incidents. Whether you were hurt commuting through town, running errands, or passing through on SR-4, the aftermath can mean medical bills, missed work, and confusing calls from an insurance adjuster. We're a personal injury law practice that handles car accident claims for injured Brentwood residents and visitors. We can evaluate what happened and explain your options. Early steps matter: preserving photos, witness information, and vehicle damage evidence before it disappears can make a real difference later. You don't have to sort through this alone or guess what an insurer's offer is actually worth. A quick, no-cost conversation with our team can help clarify where you stand.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Settling

items.title: California's Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury lawsuit in California, but claims against a government entity — say, for a road issue on Sand Creek Road — can require notice in as little as six months.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce Your Recovery
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning even if you're partly blamed for a Brentwood Boulevard collision, you can still recover damages reduced by your share of fault — but insurers often try to inflate that share.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Recover
items.desc: We work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to find out where you stand, and non-economic damages like pain and suffering aren't capped under California law.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters often ask questions designed to get you to downplay your injuries or accept partial fault. Our team can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: What if my crash happened on SR-4 or another state highway near Brentwood?
items.answer: Crashes on state routes can sometimes involve claims against a government entity, which may carry a much shorter notice deadline than the standard two-year statute of limitations. It's worth having our team review the specifics quickly so you don't miss a filing window.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: Nothing. Our team typically works on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no obligation to move forward after your initial conversation.
